title: Grapes Emoji 🍇 Meaning: Wine, Luxury and TikTok Slang
description: 🍇 stands for grapes, wine and indulgence. On TikTok, “grape” is also a euphemism for sexual assault. Learn the grapes emoji's meanings and how to read them.
summary: The 🍇 grapes emoji means the fruit, vineyards and wine, and it suggests abundance or luxury. It is used for snacks, charcuterie boards and New Year traditions. On TikTok, “grape” and this emoji also serve as a euphemism for rape in content that discusses sexual assault.
meaning: A bunch of purple grapes has meant plenty for a very long time. The fruit belongs to Dionysus and Bacchus, the ancient gods of wine, and to the image of someone reclining while being fed grapes. That is why 🍇 can suggest pampering and indulgence as well as food. Day to day it marks lunchbox snacks, cheese boards, juice, jelly and, above all, wine: tastings, vineyard weekends and harvest season.

Wine people use it as an identity marker. Sommeliers, wineries and wine-club accounts place 🍇 beside 🍷 to refer to varietals and the growing side of the business. Travelers add it to Napa, Tuscany or Bordeaux photos. In Spain and much of Latin America, eating twelve grapes at the stroke of midnight on New Year's Eve is a good-luck ritual, and the emoji floods feeds at that moment each year.

There is also a serious coded meaning. On TikTok and similar apps, creators avoid the word “rape” because it can get videos restricted, and “grape” became the common substitute, written out or as 🍇. Survivors telling their stories, true-crime accounts and advocates all use it. The term is not meant as humor. Seeing 🍇 in a caption about assault, safety or a court case signals that subject.

contexts.label: In food and wine posts
contexts.body: The largest share of use is literal. It tags picnic spreads, wine flights and grocery hauls, and it pairs with 🧀 for a charcuterie board. Wineries use it for harvest updates in late summer and fall. A caption like “grape expectations 🍇” is the kind of pun it invites.

contexts.label: On TikTok
contexts.body: Take a moment to read the caption. If the video concerns abuse, consent or a criminal case, 🍇 is standing in for a word the creator cannot safely type. Related forms include “graped” and “SA.” Replying with jokes about fruit under such a video would be badly out of place.

contexts.label: On holidays
contexts.body: On New Year's Eve, Spanish-speaking users post 🍇 for las doce uvas, the twelve grapes eaten with the midnight chimes. The custom has spread on social media, including a version done under a table for luck in love. It also appears at Thanksgiving and harvest celebrations as a symbol of abundance.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Privately the emoji is a snack, a drink plan or a little luxury joke: “feed me 🍇” means “spoil me.” It is occasionally used as crude slang for testicles, mainly among friends joking around. It has no standard flirtatious meaning.

examples.text: Wine tasting in Sonoma this weekend 🍇🍷
12 grapes at midnight, manifesting a good year 🍇✨
examples.meaning: Taking part in the New Year's Eve good-luck tradition.

examples.text: Day off. Someone come fan me and feed me 🍇
examples.meaning: A joke about wanting to be pampered like royalty.

examples.text: TW: 🍇. Sharing my story because it might help someone
examples.meaning: A content warning for a discussion of sexual assault.

examples.text: Built a whole board for girls night 🍇🧀🥖

combos.meaning: Wine, winemaking or a vineyard visit.
The twelve grapes of New Year's Eve.
Living luxuriously, or wanting to be treated like royalty.

confusedWith.difference: 🍷 is the finished drink and signals relaxing, dinner or a night out. 🍇 points to the fruit and the vineyard, and it works for non-drinkers and children in a way the glass does not.
🫐 shows a few round blue berries with leaves and can look like grapes at small sizes. Blueberries mean breakfast and baking and carry none of the wine or luxury associations.
🍒 is also clustered fruit on stems, but red, and it has flirtatious and lucky meanings. Grapes are tied to wine and plenty instead.

avoid: Don't joke with 🍇 under posts where it is being used to discuss sexual assault.
Avoid the “grape” euphemism in formal reporting, support resources or anywhere clear language is needed.
Be aware that sending it alone to a TikTok-savvy friend could be momentarily misread.
design: The emoji shows a full cluster of grapes hanging in a rough triangle, with a stem and often a green leaf at the top. Nearly every vendor colors them purple, in shades from violet to deep wine. There is no green-grape version. The designs are consistent enough that it is recognized instantly on any device.

faqs.a: It is a substitute for the word “rape.” Because the platform may limit videos that use the original term, people write “grape” or use 🍇 when discussing sexual violence. It is a workaround for moderation, used in serious contexts.

faqs.q: What does 🍇 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: In ordinary chats, fruit, wine or a joke about being pampered. It is not a flirting staple. If it appears with a content warning or in a heavy conversation, the sender may be referring to assault using the TikTok euphemism.

faqs.q: Why do people eat 12 grapes on New Year's?
faqs.a: It is a Spanish tradition, also common across Latin America, of eating one grape with each of the twelve midnight chimes to bring luck for each month ahead. Social media has popularized it widely, and 🍇 is its emoji.

faqs.q: Is there a green grapes emoji?
faqs.a: No. The single grapes emoji is purple on all major platforms. People use it for any grape variety, or pair it with a green heart or the word itself if color matters.

faqs.q: When was the grapes emoji added?
faqs.a: It has been around since the original emoji set was standardized in 2010 and sits first in the fruit section of most emoji keyboards.
